name: Intestinal Disease Due to Vitamin Absorption Anomaly

criteria.description: Presence of clinical signs consistent with vitamin deficiency (e.g., neurological or hematological manifestations)
Documented low serum levels of one or more vitamins despite adequate dietary intake
Evidence of intestinal malabsorption demonstrated by specialized tests (e.g., D-xylose test, Schilling test, or biopsy)
Identification of mutations in genes related to vitamin absorption pathways (if available)
Clinical and biochemical improvement following targeted vitamin supplementation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: clinical signs of vitamin deficiency, documented low serum vitamin levels, and evidence of intestinal malabsorption
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing and response to supplementation support diagnosis but are not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Pernicious anemia due to vitamin B12 malabsorption
searchTerms: low red blood cells due to B12 malabsorption

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neurological manifestations of vitamin B12 deficiency (e.g., subacute combined degeneration)
searchTerms: nerve problems from vitamin B12 lack
neurological symptoms like numbness or weakness
spinal cord degeneration from B12 deficiency

common.symptomName: Glossitis associated with vitamin B deficiency
searchTerms: inflamed tongue from vitamin B deficiency

common.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy related to vitamin E or B12 deficiency
searchTerms: nerve damage from vitamin E or B12 deficiency

common.symptomName: Muscle weakness secondary to vitamin D deficiency
searchTerms: muscle weakness from vitamin D deficiency
low muscle strength due to vitamin lack

common.symptomName: Easy bruising due to vitamin K deficiency
searchTerms: easy bruising from vitamin K lack
bleeding tendency due to vitamin K deficiency

occasional.symptomName: Ophthalmological disturbances such as night blindness from vitamin A deficiency
searchTerms: eye problems like night blindness from vitamin A deficiency
vision disturbances related to vitamin A

occasional.symptomName: Bone pain or osteomalacia related to vitamin D deficiency
searchTerms: bone pain from vitamin D deficiency

occasional.symptomName: Recurrent infections due to impaired immune function from vitamin deficiencies
searchTerms: frequent infections due to poor immunity

rare.symptomName: Cardiovascular abnormalities related to vitamin B1 (thiamine) deficiency
searchTerms: cardiovascular symptoms due to vitamin B1 lack
heart failure related to vitamin B1 deficiency

rare.symptomName: Dermatological manifestations such as dermatitis from vitamin B3 (niacin) deficiency
searchTerms: dermatitis due to vitamin B3 lack

rare.symptomName: Psychiatric symptoms including depression or cognitive impairment
searchTerms: mental health symptoms like low mood

laboratory: Low serum levels of vitamins B12, D, E, A, and K
Macrocytic anemia on complete blood count
Elevated methylmalonic acid and homocysteine levels
imaging: MRI showing spinal cord demyelination in subacute combined degeneration
Bone densitometry indicating osteopenia or osteomalacia
genetic: Mutations in genes encoding intrinsic factor, cubilin, or other vitamin transporters
other: Positive Schilling test indicating impaired vitamin B12 absorption
Histological evidence of villous atrophy or mucosal abnormalities on intestinal biopsy

distinguishingFeatures: Histological findings of villous atrophy with crypt hyperplasia

redFlags: Rapid onset of neurological deficits such as paresthesia or ataxia
Severe macrocytic anemia with neurological symptoms
references: Orphanet: Intestinal disease due to vitamin absorption anomaly, ORPHA:104004
